counterexample: k = 3 (111 vs 0111): the average over n <= 2^40 is 0.2282 against the prediction 0.2875 of (a) (EXP-C11-06); the running average is 0.228181, 0.309709 and 0.228548 at N = 2^40, 2^80 and 2^120, so it does not converge (EXP-C11-07). Both statements hold only for k = 2 (value 1).
statement:
(a) The average over n <= N of L_(1^k)(n) - L_u(n), u unbordered of length k + 1, tends to log_lambda(1/(lambda - 1)).
(b) Corrected version: this average converges to (2 - lambda)/(lambda - 1)^2.
title: Average gain of an unbordered terminator over 1^k: log_lambda(1/(lambda-1)), then convergence to (2-lambda)/(lambda-1)^2 (both refuted)
